source.title: Classification and Adversarial examples in an Overparameterized Linear Model: A Signal Processing Perspective
source.authors: Adhyyan Narang; Vidya K. Muthukumar; Anant Sahai

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including appendices. Some symbols are garbled in the text extraction, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes classification generalization in overparameterized feature models using a different model and method from the claim versions. It does not test the specified random-label, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, or network-sharpness comparisons.
record.gate_note: The study reports classification risk for minimum-norm interpolators on synthetic constant-label data, with interpolation implying zero training error. These results bear on generalization but do not test whether a model that fits random labels also generalizes on natural labels under standard gradient training. Adversarial-risk and regression results are outside the claim’s stated scope.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes classification and adversarial risk in minimum-norm Fourier and polynomial feature models on synthetic constant-label data. None of its results tests V1–V8. Its width-dependent RFS results concern random linear combinations of fixed Fourier features, rather than the trained ReLU networks named in V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: structured lifted-feature minimum-norm interpolators can achieve vanishing classification risk despite poor regression performance, while remaining vulnerable to shrinking input perturbations. The authors also establish convergence of sufficiently wide RFS models to the Fourier model and demonstrate classification double descent.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic one-dimensional feature-lifting model with a minimum-norm interpolator; it does not use the specified image or language benchmarks or standard gradient-training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Classification risk varies with q and feature family; the paper reports different behavior for independent features and lifted Fourier or Legendre features.

fits_no_version.finding: For the regularly spaced, constant-label Fourier model, classification risk tends to zero for q < p, including regimes with poor regression performance. Legendre and randomly sampled Fourier experiments show related decreasing-error trends.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-norm interpolation can generalize in constant-label classification with suitable structured feature maps and feature weighting, despite poor regression performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports asymptotic Fourier classification risk 1/2 when q > p.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification consistency in this Fourier model fails when weighting insufficiently favors the true constant feature.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 and Figure 4 report classification double descent as the number of random-Fourier-sum features increases with n = 40 and p = 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the number of random linear combinations of fixed Fourier features can reduce classification test error beyond interpolation in a minimum-norm constant-label model.

record.problems: The main analysis uses a stylized one-dimensional synthetic setup with constant labels and regularly spaced training points; the authors describe the random-training-data calculation as heuristic. Empirical results in the supplied figures provide no extracted numerical uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Adversarial classification-risk results and regression-risk results are omitted because the claim explicitly separates adversarial behavior and concerns the training-to-test classification gap. The RFS-feature results about double descent and distance of errors from training points are also omitted because they do not test one of the mapped versions or directly report the claimed natural-label generalization behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its comparison with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error after widening trained one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the width needed for zero training error. RFS random-feature width results concern a different system.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning scope, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps or ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row measures a different effect; this does not negate the reported classification results. The RFS results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows. Table 1's independent-feature results are comparisons to earlier work.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on fixed random labels or compare held-out random-label accuracy; the data use a constant true labeling function and a minimum-norm interpolator, not the specified architectures and training recipes.
Does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, or isolate widening beyond the interpolation threshold as specified.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or test local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or vary optimizer tuning.
Does not compare batch sizes or training budgets.
Does not test dropout or its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
Does not identify or remove memorized training examples.
